title: Adani Cement Begins Deployment of Electric Trucks, Plans to Operate Over 2,000 EVs by 2030

read.desc: The company has flagged off its first fleet of heavy-duty electric trucks at the Sanghi Plant in Gujarat, aiming to reduce logistics emissions by over 25,000 tonnes of CO₂ annually.
paras: The company has flagged off its first fleet of heavy-duty electric trucks at the Sanghi Plant in Gujarat, aiming to reduce logistics emissions by over 25,000 tonnes of CO₂ annually. Adani Cement, part of the Adani Group, has flagged off its first fleet of heavy-duty electric trucks at its Sanghi Plant in Gujarat, marking a significant step towards decarbonising its cement and clinker transportation operations. As part of its first-phase deployment plan, the company aims to introduce 410 electric trucks by March 2027. The fleet is expected to reduce more than 25,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions annually and replace approximately 11 million litres of diesel consumption each year. The company has also outlined an ambitious long-term target of shifting 10% of its road logistics volume to electric trucks by 2030, with plans to deploy more than 2,000 electric vehicles (EVs) across its operations. EV Deployment to Strengthen Green Logistics Commenting on the initiative, Vinod Bahety, CEO - Cement Business, Adani Group , said the deployment at Sanghi marks the beginning of a broader transition towards electric transportation. The company has identified multiple routes across India for the movement of clinker and cement through EV-based logistics. He added that electrifying its truck fleet would help reduce the company's carbon footprint while limiting its exposure to fluctuations in diesel prices. According to Bahety, the initiative combines sustainability with operational efficiency and supports the company's ambition to build a greener and more competitive cement business. The company said that powering electric trucks through renewable energy can help eliminate freight-related emissions, contributing to its Scope 3 emission reduction strategy and long-term net-zero goals. Falling Battery Costs Improve EV Economics The economic viability of heavy-duty electric trucks in India's cement sector has improved over the past decade. According to the company, diesel prices have increased by around 60%, while lithium-ion battery pack costs have declined by approximately 70%. Solar tariffs have also fallen by 47% during the same period. Diesel-powered trucks emit approximately 0.7375 kg of CO₂ per kilometre. In comparison, electric trucks powered by renewable energy can eliminate up to 100% of these freight-related emissions, making transportation electrification an important lever for reducing Scope 3 emissions. The proposed fleet of 410 electric trucks is expected to deliver annual carbon savings of more than 25,000 tonnes. Adani Cement plans to expand the initiative to additional routes and manufacturing plants as part of its broader green logistics strategy. Addressing Emissions Across Cement Supply Chains India is the world's second-largest cement producer with the transportation of limestone, clinker and finished cement forming a significant part of the industry's supply chain. However, the movement of these materials across long distances also contributes to the sector's overall carbon footprint. Through its electric truck deployment, Adani Cement aims to address both the environmental and operational challenges associated with conventional diesel-powered transportation. The initiative is expected to support cleaner freight movement, improve logistics efficiency and reduce dependence on fossil fuels. The deployment also aligns with the company's broader sustainability commitments, as it works towards integrating renewable energy and low-emission transportation solutions across its cement manufacturing and distribution network.

paras: Shareholding has emerged as a sticking point in Adani Defence & Aerospace’s negotiations with Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer over the structure of their proposed joint venture (JV) to manufacture civilian aircraft in India, industry sources told businessline .

The discussions centre on a proposed structure under which Adani would hold 49 per cent of the new entity, while Embraer owns the remaining 51 per cent. Embraer has maintained during the discussions that it requires a 51 per cent stake to ensure full compliance with its quality assurance and technology transfer requirements. However, Adani wants a 51:49 split in its favour.
Neither Adani Defence & Aerospace nor Embraer India responded to a request for comments.
The two sides are seeking to work out a mutually acceptable formula as they pursue plans to manufacture regional aircraft in India.

Senior executives from Embraer, including its top leadership, have visited New Delhi several times over the past few months to meet officials of the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA). The company has cited a similar 49:51 shareholding arrangement in its overseas joint ventures, where it retains the majority stake, said sources. The company has also maintained that the proposed ownership model follows the structure used in the defence space.

The fishing community there urged the Tamil Nadu State Coastal Zone Management Authority to reject the port's request for exemption from a public hearing and not recommend coastal regulation zone clearance in its present form, and also demanded a fresh public hearing near the fishing village.

title: India: Adani signs 3-year copper supply deal with Attero

read.desc: Attero will supply 72,000 t of recycled anodes over 3 years Deal expected to cut Adani
paras: Adani Enterprises has reportedly signed a three-year copper supply agreement with Noida-based recycler Attero. The company will procure copper anodes for its Kutch Copper facility in Mundra, Gujarat. As part of the deal, Attero will supply 2,000 t monthly. This translates into 24,000 t annually and 72,000 t over three years. Sources familiar with the matter estimate the deal's value at around $1 billion.

The agreement was signed three months ago. It is expected to reduce Adani's imported feedstock dependence by approximately 5%. Attero will recover copper from electronic waste and discarded batteries to produce the anodes. Consequently, Kutch Copper will gain an additional domestic feedstock source. The arrangement comes amid persistent tightness in global copper concentrate availability.

Adani entered India's copper industry in March 2024. Its subsidiary, Kutch Copper, commissioned the first phase of its Mundra smelting complex. The facility was designed to produce 500,000 t annually. The company invested approximately $1.2 billion in this phase.

Government data highlight Kutch Copper's gradual production ramp up. The company produced 8,000 t of cathodes in CY24, rising to 33,300 t during January-October 2025. Its output increased further to 112,000 t in FY26. More recently, the smelter operated at 64% utilisation during Q2FY27 (July-September 2026).
Adani now plans a second phase to raise the complex's total annual refining capacity to 1 mnt. Upon completion, the facility could become the world's largest single-location custom copper smelter.

title: Adani Cement plans 410 electric trucks in india as freight economics shift

read.desc: Adani Cement targets 410 battery electric trucks by March 2027 amid shifting diesel and battery costs.
paras: Heavy road haulage has long been one of the hardest links in India's cement supply chain to decarbonise. Limestone, clinker and bagged cement require high-payload transport over demanding routes. Adani Cement is moving to shift a share of that workload onto electric power.

The company flagged off its initial electric haulage trucks at the Sanghi facility in Gujarat in mid-November 2026. These vehicles will move clinker and finished cement along active industrial corridors. Spanning brands such as Ambuja Cements, ACC and Orient Cement, the producer holds more than 113 million tonnes of annual installed capacity.

Management views the rollout as an early step toward electrifying 10% of its road logistics volume. That goal equates to over 2,000 electric trucks by 2030. The firm points to a structural tipping point in freight economics rather than a purely environmental gesture.

Higher diesel expenses, lower lithium-ion battery costs and falling solar tariffs are narrowing the operating gap for heavy electric trucks. Company estimates indicate that the 410-truck fleet could displace roughly 11 million litres of diesel each year. It could also cut carbon dioxide emissions by more than 25,000 tonnes annually when paired with renewable electricity.

Diesel trucks are calculated to emit about 0.7375 kilograms of carbon dioxide per kilometre. Scaling electric heavy-duty freight across sprawling plant networks still tests charging availability, turnaround times and grid readiness along long-haul routes.

title: Adani to shut down 800MW unit from midnight

paras: Maintenance work to continue until 18 December; the power plant’s generation capacity will be halved during the period An 800-megawatt unit of Adani Power’s Godda power plant in India’s Jharkhand state will be shut down from midnight on Wednesday, 25 November, for annual maintenance. The unit is scheduled to remain out of operation until 18 December, while the plant’s other 800MW unit will continue generating electricity as usual, the Indian company said. In a statement sent to the media on Wednesday, Adani Power said the maintenance had been planned in advance as part of the plant’s routine maintenance programme. The Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) approved the plan on 26 October. The work will include inspection and servicing of essential equipment, as well as measures to prevent potential technical faults in the future. The coal-fired Godda power plant has a total generation capacity of 1,600MW, with each of its two units capable of producing 800MW. However, under the power purchase agreement, the plant is required to supply a combined 1,496MW to Bangladesh. With one unit offline, the plant’s capacity to supply electricity to Bangladesh will be reduced by half during the maintenance period. In November 2017, the BPDB signed a 25-year power purchase agreement with Adani Power Jharkhand Limited. Under the deal, Adani built the Godda power plant at a cost of around $2 billion to supply electricity to Bangladesh. Power from its first unit began flowing into Bangladesh’s national grid on 9 March 2023. The maintenance shutdown comes as electricity demand in Bangladesh begins to decline with the onset of winter. According to data from the National Load Dispatch Centre (NLDC), electricity imports from India rose by around 37% in the first 15 days of November compared with the same period in October, despite a decline in domestic electricity demand and generation. Bangladesh imported an average of 33.6 million units of electricity a day during the first half of October. The daily average rose to 46 million units in the corresponding period of November. Mohammad Zahurul Islam, a BPDB member for generation, told bdnews24.com at the time that imports had increased because generating electricity from furnace oil was more expensive than importing power. Adani’s power supply to Bangladesh has previously been disrupted by technical faults and coal shortages. On 10 September, the plant’s second unit was shut down following a technical fault. It resumed generation three days later, on 13 September. NLDC data show that Adani supplied 1,430.06MW during the evening peak demand period on 9 September. After one unit was taken offline on 10 September, supply fell to 691.44MW.

title: Kenya’s exit from cancelled Adani power deal could cost $339mn, Treasury estimates

read.desc: Kenya’s National Treasury has estimated that terminating its cancelled power transmission agreement with India’s Adani Energy Solutions NSE:ADANIENSOL could cost KES43.94bn ($339mn), more than the estimated KES41bn ($317mn) cost of building the two lines included in the estimate.The estimate appear…
paras: ADANIENSOL Kenya’s National Treasury has estimated that terminating its cancelled power transmission agreement with India’s Adani Energy Solutions ADANIENSOL could cost KES43.94bn ($339mn), more than the estimated KES41bn ($317mn) cost of building the two lines included in the estimate.

The estimate appears in the Treasury’s fifth annual report on the state of public-private partnerships (PPPs) in Kenya, covering the year to June 2026, according to Billionaires.Africa and People Daily . The report presents the figure as an estimated termination payment and a contingent liability, not an amount currently due.

The estimate covers the 400kV Lessos–Loosuk line and the 220kV Kisumu (Kibos)–Kakamega–Musaga line, which together were expected to cost about KES41bn to build, according to Billionaires.Africa . State-owned Kenya Electricity Transmission Company (KETRACO) signed the 30-year agreement with Adani in October 2024 for three power lines, valued at $736mn at the time.

President William Ruto directed the cancellation of the transmission contract, together with a separate Adani proposal to take over and expand Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, on November 21, 2024, after US prosecutors indicted Adani Group founder Gautam Adani over an alleged bribery scheme in India. The Adani Group has denied the allegations.

Termination began in the 2024/25 financial year and remained under way at the end of June 2026. KETRACO and the Treasury’s PPP Directorate are pursuing a mutual separation that would settle verified costs Adani incurred before the deal was ended. The report does not disclose the costs Adani has submitted or any payments made, Business.co.ke reported.

title: Cementing Cement Powerhouse Position: Karan Adani's Bold Gambit

The larger challenge, however, was integrating these legacy businesses and competing in a fiercely competitive market. Under Karan Adani's leadership, the focus has evolved from building scale to creating an integrated building materials platform positioned for long-term growth and operational efficiency.

The transformation reflects Karan's approach to growth: ambitious in intent, but increasingly disciplined in execution. From a base of approximately 67.55 MTPA at the time of the Holcim India acquisition, Adani Cement has expanded rapidly through a combination of greenfield and brownfield projects and strategic acquisitions, including Sanghi Industries, Penna Cement, Orient Cement, Asian Cement and My Home Group's Tuticorin grinding unit. Today, the business is at around 110 MTPA of capacity, giving the Group national scale, deeper market access, long-term limestone security and significant strategic optionality.
In a business of this scale, execution discipline is as important as expansion ambition. This footprint provides the foundation for its next phase of value driven- "One Cement Platform".

That is why the near-term priority is clear: complete projects already under execution, strengthen engineering readiness before starting new ones, improve plant reliability, optimise the manufacturing and logistics footprint, and stabilise the assets that have recently entered the system. Sanghi, for instance, brings a strategic coastal advantage and over time can play a more optimised role in the company's clinker, grinding and logistics architecture. Penna and Orient add complementary regional strength and capacity depth. The real value of these acquisitions will be unlocked when they are fully integrated into one operating platform.

title: Vizhinjam port starts first major import cargo movement to Kottayam inland depot

paras: Vizhinjam International Seaport has begun its first major import cargo movement to the Kottayam Inland Container Depot, moving about 1,500 tonnes of African natural rubber in 60 containers for tyre maker MRF. The tyre company chose Vizhinjam as its port of destination to avoid transhipment through Mumbai, which could take up to a month. The empty containers will then be kept at Kottayam for exporters, cutting the cost of bringing empties from Kochi. Officials say the link could help the depot grow into a competitive regional logistics hub.

Thiruvananthapuram: Vizhinjam International Seaport Ltd (VISL) said on Saturday that the movement of 60 containers carrying around 1,500 tonnes of natural rubber, imported from Africa for MRF, from Vizhinjam to the Kottayam Inland Container Depot (ICD) is expected to give a major boost to cargo operations. The consignment covers 20 containers under each of three bills of lading. VISL said this is the first major import cargo movement from Vizhinjam to the Kottayam depot and a significant step in the depot's development. The tyre maker chose Vizhinjam as its port of destination to avoid transhipment through Mumbai, which could take up to a month, VISL said. At the Kottayam ICD, the containers will undergo customs examination and other clearance procedures. After Customs Out of Charge clearance, the same trucks will take them to MRF's centralised warehouse in Kochi, which is expected to speed up the availability of raw material for the company's factories. The empties can then be stored at the Kottayam container yard for exporters. At present, exporters often bring empty containers from Kochi to Kottayam to load cargo, and reusing import empties would cut that cost and time, VISL said. ICD Kottayam said the triangulation of import and export movements is expected to create a cost-effective logistics ecosystem and make it a more competitive regional hub. VISL said the move is in line with Mission Samudra, an initiative conceived under the Chief Minister to strengthen Keralam's maritime trade, and credited Ports Secretary Rathan U Kelkar and Keralam Maritime Board Chief Executive Officer and VISL Managing Director Geromic George with improving the depot's facilities. Vizhinjam, operated by Adani Ports, is India's first semi-automated container port and one of the few in South Asia able to berth ultra-large container vessels, according to New Kerala. The port handled 1.3 million TEUs in FY26, Devdiscourse reported, citing the company. In September 2026, it handled 17,262 TEUs from a single call by MSC Loreto, a record for the port, India Shipping News reported. The port is also preparing to grow. Maritime Gateway reported that the Kerala government and Adani Ports announced Phase 2 plans in January 2026, with an investment of INR 16,000 crore to raise capacity from 1 million to 5.7 million TEUs. Much of Vizhinjam's early volume came from transhipment, with trade publication The Loadstar reporting at the end of its first year that relay volumes came from its lone mainline customer, MSC. Inland gateway cargo, such as the MRF consignment, is a different line of business for the port. The statements did not give the expected cost saving for MRF or say how many further consignments are planned through the Kottayam depot. Source: PTI

title: Maharashtra pollution board halts Adani's excavation work at 1,500 MW Tarali project site

Mumbai: The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) has directed Adani Renewable Energy One Ltd to immediately stop excavation and construction activities for a temporary labour camp and storage facilities at Sawarghar village in Patan taluka of Satara district. The work is associated with the company's proposed 1,500 MW Tarali Pumped Storage Project. In a notice dated November 20, the board said the company had undertaken excavation and site development without informing it or obtaining the required permissions and environmental clearance. The notice covers work at Gat Nos. 33 and 34 in Sawarghar, where land was being developed for a temporary labour camp and other storage activities. The MPCB said its officials inspected the site on November 20, after which the Satara sub-regional officer submitted a proposal for legal action. The board directed the company to stop all ongoing and proposed excavation and construction work and not resume any activity without its prior permission. It warned that non-compliance could invite action under environmental laws. The directions were issued under Section 33A of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and Section 31A of the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. The MPCB said the company had not secured environmental clearance from the competent authority for the excavation and development work. The board's notice acknowledged that it had granted consent for the 1,500 MW standalone pumped storage project in April 2025, subject to specified terms and conditions. However, the permission for the main project did not remove the requirement to obtain the necessary approvals for the activities being undertaken at the Sawarghar plots. An Adani spokesperson said the MPCB communication related specifically to Gat Nos. 33 and 34, which had been earmarked for temporary construction-support facilities and were not part of the permanent project components. The company said the permanent components of the Tarali project had the requisite statutory clearances. It added that the temporary use of the private land had been considered in the layout approved by the Central Electricity Authority. The spokesperson said the company was submitting its response to the MPCB with relevant facts and clarifications. In the interim, activities at the two plots had been kept in abeyance. The company also said the temporary facilities would be dismantled after construction and the land restored, as applicable. The MPCB's action follows a separate direction from the Maharashtra Forest Department on November 13 to stop work on the Tarali project over the absence of prior approval from the National Board for Wildlife. Adani had said the project did not involve notified protected areas or forest land and that its proposal relating to wildlife clearance had been submitted to the competent authority. The Tarali project is proposed on the Tarali dam reservoir in Satara district. The latest MPCB order is specific to the temporary facilities at Sawarghar; it does not state that all work across the pumped storage project has been stopped. Source- PTI

paras: Lucknow: How did a 50-year agreement granting a private company rights to operate, manage and develop a major international airport get executed on a stamp certificate worth just ₹500? And why did subsequent government assessments put the potential stamp duty shortfall at ₹249.63 crore? These are among the questions arising from the concession agreement for Lucknow's Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport, involving the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and Adani Lucknow International Airport Limited.

An investigation by New Delhi Post , based on official records obtained from the Uttar Pradesh Stamp Department, has uncovered a substantial discrepancy between the stamp duty paid when the agreement was executed and the liability subsequently assessed by government officials. The findings also bring the valuation of thousands of crores of rupees in airport land, the classification of the agreement and the treatment of public assets under scrutiny.

The concession agreement was signed on February 14, 2020, between the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and Adani Lucknow International Airport Limited. It covered 1,258.80 acres of airport land and granted the private concessionaire rights relating to the airport's operation, management and development for 50 years.

Yet, the original e-stamp certificate classified the document under Article 5 – General Agreement. The property description was recorded as 'Not Applicable', the consideration was shown as zero, and the stamp duty paid was just ₹500.

This raises a fundamental question: how was an agreement involving long-term commercial rights over a major public infrastructure asset treated as a general agreement rather than a document attracting stamp duty based on the nature and value of the rights being granted?

title: Adani Cement to deploy 410 heavy-duty electric trucks

paras: Indian cement manufacturer Adani Cement (Adani Group) has announced plans to add 410 heavy-duty electric trucks to its fleet. It has already flagged off the first batch as part of the initiative and will commission the remaining trucks by March 2027.

Based on images shared with the announcement, Adani Cement appears to have procured eleven units initially. The company has deployed these heavy-duty electric trucks at its Sanghi plant in the western state of Gujarat and is using them to transport clinker and cement. It says the movement of both these materials is a carbon-intensive part of the cement industry’s operations.

The first batch comprises Chinese manufacturer Sany’s 55-tonne heavy-duty electric trucks. These units appear to be either the 5538E or the 5550E, the two 55-tonne high-roof models the company offers in India, both of which have a 4×2 drivetrain layout and pack 360 kW of power. The 5538E uses a 282 kWh battery pack that supports charging at up to 240 kW and delivers a range of 189 km. The 5550E upgrades to a 376 kWh battery pack that supports charging at up to 360 kW and increases the range to 245 km.

Adani Cement says the economics are now in favour of electric trucks in India’s cement industry. The company says that while diesel prices have increased by 60 per cent over the past decade, lithium-ion battery pack costs and solar tariffs have fallen by approximately 70 per cent and 47 per cent, respectively. It also states that diesel trucks emit approximately 737.5 grams of CO2 per kilometre. The company estimates its 410 electric trucks will reduce its diesel consumption by 11 million litres per year and avoid more than 25,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions annually.

Vinod Bahety, CEO of the Cement Business at Adani Group, said the company has identified multiple routes across the country for transporting clinker and cement using electric trucks. Its plan to deploy 410 electric trucks by March 2027 represents the first phase of electrifying these transport operations. By 2030, the company aims to expand its fleet to over 2,000 electric trucks and use them to handle 10 per cent of its road freight.

In a recent development, the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) has issued an order allowing the Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution Co. Ltd. (CSPDCL) to amend its petition involving a substantial ₹85.28 crore safeguard duty claim against Adani Solar Energy Jaisalmer One Pvt. Ltd. The core of the dispute traces back to the imposition and subsequent removal of safeguard duty (SGD) on imported solar cells, a fiscal element that directly impacts project economics and power purchase agreement (PPA) tariffs.

CSPDCL procures power from Adani Solar’s 450 MW solar project located in Rajasthan through an intermediary agreement with the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI). The state distribution company contends that the expiration and removal of the 15% safeguard duty effective from 30 July 2021 constitutes a ‘Change in Law’ event under the PPA terms. According to CSPDCL, this regulatory shift reduced Adani Solar’s operational costs, and the resulting financial benefit should rightfully be passed on to the consumers in Chhattisgarh through a lower tariff or a direct refund of ₹85.28 crore along with applicable interest.

During the proceedings, CSPDCL sought to amend its petition to include a government notification dated 30 July 2018, correcting references that previously only highlighted a later notification from 29 July 2020. Adani Solar strongly opposed the amendment, arguing that the request was time-barred beyond the three-year limitation period, relied on assumptions rather than actual costs, and that the expiry of the 2018 notification was anticipated. However, CERC dismissed Adani’s objections as hyper-technical, classifying the amendment as a clarification rather than a novel case that prejudices the developer, while noting that Adani remains free to contest the substantive merits during the main hearings.

paras: Adani Airport Holdings (AAHL) has entered into an agreement with 360 ONE Alternates Asset Management for a Rs 2,790 crore primary equity investment, strengthening its capital base as it pursues a substantial expansion of aviation infrastructure and airport-linked commercial assets.

The transaction values AAHL at a pre-money valuation of about USD 18 billion and takes the airport operator’s aggregate equity mobilisation to approximately USD 1.35 billion. AAHL will issue fresh shares to 360 ONE Asset at the same valuation and on the same terms agreed with investors that participated in its preceding capital raise.

The latest investment follows the Rs 9,825 crore equity infusion announced earlier this year by a consortium comprising Alpha Wave Global, Premji Invest, Temasek and funds managed by BlackRock. The transaction marked AAHL’s first major institutional equity raise from a group of global investors.

The earlier investors committed the capital through a three-tranche arrangement. Upon completion of that transaction, the investors are expected to hold a collective 5.54 per cent stake in AAHL. With 360 ONE Asset joining the shareholder group, investors participating in the two transactions are expected to hold an aggregate stake of approximately 7.01 per cent in AAHL.

Expansion Remains Capital Priority The successive equity transactions come as AAHL undertakes a broad-based expansion of its airport portfolio. The company is targeting annual passenger-handling capacity of 200 million, compared with its historical capacity of around 96 million. The capital will support the expansion and modernisation of airport facilities, alongside investments in infrastructure required to accommodate rising passenger volumes.

Adani Defence Successfully Fires Four Anti-Tank Missiles in Pokhran Test Range

read.desc: Adani Defence successfully tests its Bagheera AT1 anti-tank missile system at Rajasthan's Pokhran range, demonstrating day and night firing, tandem missile launches and aerial-target engagement.
paras: Pokhran: Adani Defence & Aerospace, the Adani Group's flagship defence and aerospace company, successfully demonstrated Bagheera AT1 , a vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile (ATGM) system, at the Pokhran Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan .

The programme validated day and night engagements , a two-missile tandem firing along a single beam against a target representing an armoured vehicle, and an aerial-target engagement at an extended range. It was followed by a static display of the complete system.
The No Cost No Commitment (NCNC) demonstration at Pokhran on 20 November was witnessed by senior representatives of the Indian Army, Department of Military Affairs and Ministry of Defence (MoD).

Bagheera AT1 is the outcome of 18 months of design and development , during which Adani Defence customised the missile system for Indian terrain, climate and operational requirements. The result is a complete combat system comprising the missile, automated launcher, day and night sights, mounted on an Adani Defence-designed 4x4 high-mobility armoured vehicle .
• Stand-off reach: Engages armour at up to 8 km , twice the approximately 4 km range of the land-based anti-tank missile.

paras: Manufacturing News Adani Energy Solutions Wins Bihar Transmission Project MM Desk 26/11/2026 Share Adani Energy Solutions Limited (AESL) has won a transmission project to evacuate 2,400 MW of power from the upcoming Pirpainti Ultra Super Critical Thermal Power Plant in Bihar. Awarded through the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mechanism, the project is expected to generate an annual tariff of around ₹500 crore once commissioned.

The project, titled “Evacuation of Power from 3X800 MW STPP Pirpainti”, will be implemented through a special purpose vehicle, Vikramshila Power Transmission Ltd. AESL plans to complete the project by the fourth quarter of 2028. The transmission infrastructure will support power evacuation from the Pirpainti plant and strengthen Bihar’s transmission network to improve supply reliability and meet rising electricity demand in the state.

Kandarp Patel, CEO of Adani Energy Solutions, said the project would establish a transmission system for 2,400 MW of generation capacity while strengthening Bihar’s power network. He said the infrastructure would improve grid reliability and resilience and support the state’s future power requirements.

The project will add 881 circuit kilometres of transmission lines and 3,160 MVA of transformation capacity to AESL’s portfolio. Following its completion, the company’s transmission network will increase to 30,683 circuit kilometres, with transformation capacity of 146,585 MVA. AESL’s transmission capital expenditure portfolio will reach around ₹91,500 crore.

The project involves construction of four gas-insulated substations at Jhanjharpur, Bethauli and Begusarai, along with associated transformation infrastructure. The transmission network will include 400 kV double-circuit lines connecting Pirpainti with Jhanjharpur and Begusarai, and Begusarai with Bakhtiyarpur. It will also include 220 kV double-circuit lines between Jhanjharpur and Bethauli and between Begusarai and Begusarai Town. The work also includes the line-in-line-out arrangement of existing 220 kV and 132 kV lines at Jhanjharpur and the construction of 400 kV line bays at Bakhtiyarpur Grid Substation.
